We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (p-methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (para?).

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually sulfonamide is between amine and sulfonyl chloride. Here sulfonamide connects p-tolyl-sulfonyl group to phenyl ring (the second phenyl). So we could disconnect at S-N bond: precursor: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide). That's step 1 (sulfonamide formation). Step 2: amide formation between the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline (the aniline is part of same phenyl? Actually the amide is attached to the same phenyl that is attached to sulfonyl group. The amide attaches to the phenyl via carbonyl attached to the phenyl? Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has a side chain: CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (c3). So the amide is between the cinnamic acid derivative and an aniline (c3). So we can disconnect at the amide C-N bond: precursor 1: cinnamic acid (or its derivative) and aniline (c3). That's step 2 (amide coupling). Step 3: the α,β-unsaturated acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and malonic acid to give cinnamic acid. So step 3: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). So overall 3 steps.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide -> get cinnamic acid (or trans-3-phenylacrylic acid) attached to phenyl? Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl at position of the side chain. So the cinnamic acid is attached to phenyl as substituent: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. That's 4-(trans-phenyl)acrylic acid? Actually it's phenyl attached to CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid). So we need phenyl ring (c2) with that side chain. So we can consider precursor: phenyl ring with aldehyde (c2-CHO) which via Doebner gives phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. So step 3: aromatic aldehyde (p-? maybe para to sulfonyl) + malonic acid -> cinnamic acid.

Thus final route: Step1: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and phenyl-sulfonyl-? Wait the phenyl after step2 is the phenyl bearing the side chain and aniline? Actually after step2 we have phenyl with side chain (cinnamoyl anilide). That phenyl also has sulfonyl group attached to p-tolyl via S-N. So step1: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the phenyl with side chain) which contains an NH (the aniline part? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring via N attached to sulfonyl group. In target, NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl (c1). The N is attached to the phenyl (c1) and to the sulfonyl group. So the N is part of the sulfonamide linking p-tolyl sulfonyl group to phenyl. So the phenyl side (c2) is attached to N? Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So N attached to sulfonyl group and to the tolyl phenyl (c1). So the N is part of sulfonamide linking p-tolyl phenyl (c1) to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl phenyl (c1) as an aniline (the N is attached to that phenyl). So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonyl chloride is R-SO2-Cl. Here R is p-tolyl (Cc1ccc...). So p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (the second phenyl's amine) would give the sulfonamide linking them. But the second phenyl's amine is the same N that also is attached to the tolyl phenyl? Actually the N is attached to both phenyls? In SMILES, NS(=O)(=O)c2... means N attached to sulfonyl group and to the tolyl phenyl (c1). So the N is part of the tolyl phenyl as an aniline (attached to that phenyl). So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (c2) as sulfonyl group, and the amine is the tolyl phenyl's amine (aniline). So step1: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl (c2) with sulfonyl chloride substituent (i.e., 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride). So we need precursor: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and 4-(cinnamoyl-anilide) phenylsulfonyl chloride.

Thus step1: sulfonamide formation (N of p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride). Step2: amide formation between cinnamic acid (attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3). Wait the aniline (c3) is attached to the amide nitrogen. So the phenyl c3 is an aniline that becomes amide. So step2: coupling of cinnamic acid with aniline (c3). That yields the side chain attached to phenyl c2 via carbonyl to aniline. So the product of step2 is phenyl c2 with side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (i.e., cinnamoyl anilide). This phenyl also has a sulfonyl chloride group (since we need to later form sulfonamide). So step2 precursor: phenyl c2 bearing sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) and the side chain (cinnamoyl anilide). So step2 product is that intermediate.

Step3: formation of cinnamic acid side chain via Doebner modification from aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid, giving phenyl-CH=CH-COOH attached to phenyl c2 (i.e., the same phenyl). So we need phenyl c2 with aldehyde substituent (para to sulfonyl chloride). So step3: Doebner modification.
